title: Query-Optimal Estimation of Unitary Channels in Diamond Distance
authors: Jeongwan Haah (Microsoft Quantum, USA), Robin Kothari (Microsoft Quantum, USA), Ryan O'Donnell (Carnegie Mellon University, USA), Ewin Tang (University of Washington, USA)
abstract: We consider process tomography for unitary quantum channels. Given access to an unknown unitary channel acting on a d-dimensional qudit, we aim to output a classical description of a unitary that is ε-close to the unknown unitary in diamond norm. We design an algorithm achieving error ε using O(d²/ε) applications of the unknown channel and only one qudit. This improves over prior results, which use O(d²/ε)⋅d/ε [via standard process tomography] or O(d²/ε)⋅√d [Yang, Renner, and Chiribella, PRL 2020] applications. To achieve this result, we introduce a simple technique to “bootstrap” an algorithm that can produce constant-error estimates to one that can produce ε-error estimates with the Heisenberg scaling. Finally, we prove a complementary lower bound showing that estimation requires Ω(d²/ε) applications, even with access to the inverse or controlled versions of the unknown unitary. This shows that our algorithm has both optimal query complexity and optimal space complexity.
